record.program_name: Roseville, Rocklin/Placer County Continuum of Care (CA-515, Homeless Resource Council of the Sierras) and HHAP, Placer County share
record.administering_agency: Homeless Resource Council of the Sierras (HRCS, CoC lead and HMIS lead for CA-515 and Nevada County CA-531); Placer County Health and Human Services (County HHAP administrative entity; homeless outreach with the City of Roseville)
record.typical_award_size: HHAP Round 6 allocations (HCD, 2024 count): Placer County $801,045.28 and the Roseville, Rocklin/Placer County CoC $855,530.14. HHAP rounds 1 to 5 brought $7.8 million to the Placer area, $2.0 million of it to the County ($1.8 million obligated, $892,207 spent by mid-2025). The County's HHAP-6 is planned for housing subsidies. 2024 point-in-time count: 702 people, 366 unsheltered, 640 year-round beds. The County and City of Roseville co-fund homeless outreach workers ($160,000 through June 2027).
record.affordability_requirement: People experiencing or at risk of homelessness; HHAP-6 requires a regionally coordinated action plan, a 10% youth set-aside and allows permanent housing capital, operating subsidies and rental assistance.
record.next_deadline: HHAP-6 funds are being contracted for FY 2026-27 through 2028-29; HRCS runs the CoC and HHAP sub-award processes and formed a Local Government Advisory Committee in 2025 to coordinate regional responses. HHAP Round 7 allocations follow the 2026-27 state budget ($900 million statewide).
record.layering_notes: placer.ca.gov (including DocumentCenter PDFs) sits behind Cloudflare and refused automated access on 2026-11-06; Board items were read from the County's GovDelivery agenda attachments (content.govdelivery.com/attachments/CAPLACER), the Legistar client 'placerca', state records and news coverage. Placer's HHAP is under $1 million a year each to the County and the CoC and is used for subsidies and services, not capital. For a PSH project the value is HRCS Coordinated Entry referrals and possible CoC or HHAP operating support for a few units; pair with PCHA PBVs and County in-lieu fee loans. Roseville, the largest city, has its own housing authority and homelessness programs (Pass 3).
